claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch now despite an unresolved evaluation gap in the emergency shelter placement segment, on the theory that aggregate readiness and no severity-one rehearsal incidents are sufficient and the remaining issue can be handled through documentation and ongoing monitoring.
decision_criteria: A weakness is material if it affects a contractual customer segment, protected segment, or named launch use case.
Product labels such as non-core or low-volume do not resolve materiality when the affected segment is named in customer commitments or when legal review is pending.
Material limitations for named launch use cases must be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
General evidence of aggregate readiness and monitoring can support launch posture, but cannot substitute for a missing required disclosure or approval predicate.
evidence_requests: Provide the final legal determination on whether the emergency shelter placement gap must be disclosed before launch.
Provide the actual pre-launch model-card disclosure covering this material limitation, if it has been prepared and approved.
Provide an approved risk-acceptance record that explicitly covers this named launch use case and its 1.5-point evaluation gap.
Provide evidence that the affected segment is not a named launch use case or not covered by the cited nonprofit commitments, if that is being asserted.
specific_concerns: Admissible evidence shows the emergency shelter placement segment misses target by 1.5 percentage points and is named in two nonprofit deployment commitments, which makes the weakness material under the stated policy text.

The release policy requires material limitations for named launch use cases to be disclosed unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and no such disclosure or approved risk acceptance is in evidence.
Legal review on whether disclosure is required is still open, so a required policy predicate remains unresolved.
The actor relies on aggregate readiness and general public governance guidance, but those do not satisfy the specific internal disclosure requirement for a material named launch use case.

The product note calling the segment non-core is explicitly insufficient under the policy context because low-volume labeling does not resolve materiality when customer commitments and pending legal review exist.
unsupported_claims: That the model may be certified now on the existing record without evidence of required disclosure, resolution, or approved risk acceptance.
That public model-card and AI risk-management guidance provide adequate support for certification notwithstanding the unresolved internal policy condition.
That aggregate readiness and absence of severity-one rehearsal incidents are sufficient to overcome the unresolved materiality and disclosure issue.
